best_for: Developers leaving Postman or Insomnia who want a local, offline API client, and who will buy a license once they use it for paid work.

points.title: Free for personal projects only
points.text: The source is MIT-licensed, but the prebuilt app is free only for personal use. Work use, non-profits included, needs a license: USD 79 a year or USD 349 once for an individual, and USD 149 per user per year for Business. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: 30 days to try it at work
points.text: A commercial trial starts on first launch, with no card and no sign-up. Licenses are billed yearly; there is no monthly option, and a license is tied to a Yaak account.

points.title: Five protocols in one window
points.text: It sends REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket and Server-Sent Events requests. It imports Postman, Insomnia, OpenAPI, Swagger and cURL, so moving an existing collection is a file away.

points.title: Your requests stay on your machine
points.text: Yaak says it does not store or sync your data and has no telemetry. Workspaces can be mirrored to a folder, which lets you track them in Git or sync them with Dropbox yourself.

points.title: Secrets in the keychain
points.text: Sensitive values are encrypted and can live in your OS keychain. Auth covers OAuth 2.0, JWT and Basic, and plugins can add more.

points.title: Linux is not listed here
points.text: This page lists Windows and macOS. The Windows installer is per-user (x64) and the listing keeps 46 versions; macOS has Intel and Apple silicon builds for macOS 13 and later, current release only. Linux builds come from the project itself.
